definitions.gloss: spitting image; very much alike; like two peas in a pod
definitions.explanation: Describes two people or things that look extremely similar, especially in physical appearance. Derives from the idea that when you cut a melon ({瓜|うり}) in half, the two halves look identical.

examples.japanese: {親子|おやこ}で{瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つだ。
examples.english: The parent and child are the spitting image of each other.

examples.japanese: {双子|ふたご}の{姉妹|しまい}は{瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つで{見分|みわ}けがつかない。
examples.english: The twin sisters look so alike that you can't tell them apart.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}の{母|はは}の{写真|しゃしん}を{見|み}たら、{娘|むすめ}と{瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つで{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: When I saw a photo of my mother when she was young, I was surprised at how much she looked like my daughter.

notes:
The etymology comes from cutting a {瓜|うり} (gourd/melon) in half — the two halves are perfectly identical. This is one of the most common expressions for describing a strong family resemblance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つだ — to be the spitting image
- {父親|ちちおや}と{瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つ — the spitting image of one's father
- まるで{瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つ — exactly alike

USAGE:
Most often used to describe resemblance between family members, especially parent and child. Can also be used for unrelated people who happen to look very similar. Typically used as a predicate with だ or の.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- そっくり — looking just like (more casual and broadly used; {瓜|うり}{二|ふた}つ is more vivid and literary)
- {生|い}き{写|うつ}し — a living copy (more literary; emphasizes an almost uncanny resemblance)
